amendments.body: Bug: `crates/tank_core/src/systems/plant_growth.rs:201-207` now folds Beer-Lambert depth attenuation into `plant_light_factor`, and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/algae_growth.rs:293-300` does the same for algae. That reintroduces tank-size/depth dependence into the normalization work: two tanks with identical concentrations but different fill heights no longer produce identical plant growth, which is exactly what `crates/tank_core/tests/plant_nutrient_normalization.rs:71-105` asserts. I reproduced the regression with `cargo test -p tank_core plant_limitation_is_tank_size_independent -- --nocapture`, which fails because the 10 L and 100 L tanks diverge. The same change also breaks the hand-computed algae growth contract in `crates/tank_core/tests/plant_algae_integration.rs:520-538`. This depth/turbidity coupling belongs in the later light-attenuation bead, not in the concentration-normalization bead.
amendments.rationale: This is a direct correctness regression against the task’s tank-size-independence acceptance criterion and already causes the new regression test to fail.

amendments.body: Bug: the new extinction coefficients added to `ProcessParams` at `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:171-184` are not actually configurable from process packs. `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:737-871` has no matching preset fields, `crates/tank_data/data/process/default.toml:76-87` does not expose them, and `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:424-427` hardcodes `ProcessParams::default()` for all four values. Any TOML/process-pack tuning for attenuation is therefore silently ignored, so scenario behavior depends on hidden compiled defaults instead of inspectable preset data.
amendments.rationale: The code introduces new model parameters but leaves them outside the preset/data pipeline, which makes tuning non-reproducible and violates the project requirement to keep behavior explicit and inspectable.

amendments.body: Bug: `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:774-776` gives `aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l` the alias `"aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l"`, which is just the canonical field name again. Unlike the neighboring renamed fields, it never aliases the legacy key `aob_k_tan_mg`. The custom `parse_process_params_preset` migration masks this on one internal code path, but the public `ProcessParamsPreset` deserializer no longer preserves backward compatibility for callers that use `toml::from_str` directly; those inputs fall back to the default 1.0 mg/L AOB Ks instead of the saved legacy value.
amendments.rationale: This is a concrete backward-compatibility hole in a public deserialization path, and it is easy to miss because the surrounding fields were migrated correctly.

payload.summary: Found 3 substantive issues: the new light attenuation leaks depth back into the normalization work and breaks the tank-size-independence regression, the attenuation coefficients are not plumbed through presets/process packs, and one legacy AOB preset alias is mis-specified.
